title: L/NL Regime Boundary and Transition
purpose: Define the governed boundary and transition rule between the linear and nonlinear RT operational regimes without altering RT_core.

motivation.problem: The derived linear and nonlinear regime classifications exist, but the governed boundary and transition between them is not separately classified.
motivation.resolution: L/NL change is governed as a regime-classification transition under declared orientation, residue, admissibility, and context without changing RT_core.

core_definition.lnl_boundary: The governed classification boundary between linear and nonlinear RT operational regimes.
core_definition.transition_rule: An RT operational regime transitions from L to NL when residue, history, threshold, feedback, admissibility, or context deforms local composition; it transitions from NL to L when that deformation stabilizes into a locally composable orientation.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every boundary- or transition-classified regime change must constructively trace to RT_core.

governance_rules.name: No Separate Foundations
governance_rules.statement: L and NL are not separate foundations.

governance_rules.name: Classification Not Core Change
governance_rules.statement: L/NL transition is a regime-classification change, not a change of RT_core.

governance_rules.name: Declared Boundary Evaluation
governance_rules.statement: Boundary evaluation must declare orientation, residue, admissibility, and context.

governance_rules.name: Mixed Regime Separation
governance_rules.statement: Mixed regimes are permitted only when their L and NL components are explicitly separated by domain, scale, or context.

deferred_items: Representation rules for linear algebra and nonlinear algebra
effects: Registers the governed boundary between L and NL derived regimes.
Keeps transition classification trace-bound to RT_core and orientation.
Allows mixed regimes only with explicit separation across domain, scale, or context.

notes: Existing RT, L, and NL definitions remain canonical.
Boundary and transition rules do not alter RT_core.
Future mixed-regime derivations attach under the declared boundary conditions.
The L/NL boundary is a governed classification boundary, not a replacement for RT_core.
Mixed regimes remain scope-limited until explicit separation by domain, scale, or context is declared.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
The L/NL boundary governs regime-classification change and does not supersede the canonical root expression.
